findings.where: PREREG 1 l. 22-23; 3.2 T-1 claim column l. 142; 4 T-1 HOLDS sentence l. 225 (<claim>); audit/v03/aggregate.py:21-22 (only G7 overridden, so CLAIMS['T-1'] is v0.2's, audit/aggregate.py:24-25); audit/v03/gate/t1_study.py:23
findings.quote: Within the reasonable bounds, admitting weaker evidence does not increase new false conclusions by more than δ (A1)
findings.reason: After the R1-1 decision the per-world rule tolerates max(delta, 1/n_q) (3.2 HOLDS column; checks.py:152-169). On the power study's development worlds at k = 0 the median n_q is 4 at alpha 0.90 and 12 at 0.80, so increases of 1/4 or 1/12 (up to 1/2 at n_q = 2) are tolerated. The fixed HOLDS sentence prints the claim verbatim, so a HOLDS would assert that no increase exceeded delta although larger one-atom increases were accepted: the overstatement R1-2 removed, brought back through the claim.
findings.fix: Claim: '... does not increase new false conclusions by more than δ or one wrong conclusion, whichever is larger (A1)', in 1, 3.2, a v0.3 CLAIMS['T-1'] in audit/v03/aggregate.py and the T-1 study name; then regenerate t1.cert.json (certify all --verify in step 6 needs it anyway). WordingTests then compare the new text.

findings.where: tests/test_v03_freeze.py:164-169, :182, :633; tests/test_v03_dev_run.py:306; PREREG 8 step 6 and 9 (tests/** in the manifest)
findings.quote: self.assertTrue(PC.check_status_line(ROOT))  # the working drafts are not frozen
findings.reason: Step 6 replaces both status lines and writes audit/v03/gate/GATE_TOOL.json, all frozen. Applying step 6 to a scratch copy, the two status-line tests fail (one reads the real PREREG and expects DRAFT and not frozen); with a GATE_TOOL.json present a third fails (assertFalse on its existence); once run/v03/ exists (step 8) a fourth fails. Because tests/** is frozen, the frozen suite can never pass on its own tree, and repairing it needs a new freeze. 8 never runs the suite after step 6, so the pre-freeze check does not notice. The first two came with the R1-6 repair.
findings.fix: Make the tests stage-independent: test the draft-header refusal on a header string stored in the test; for the real files require no problems if line 3 is the frozen line and problems otherwise; for GATE_TOOL.json and run/v03 compare existence and mtime before and after instead of asserting absence. Add to 8 step 6 that, after the status lines and GATE_TOOL.json are in place, the full suite runs on the tree to be frozen and must pass.

findings.where: PREREG 4 l. 222-223; audit/v03/aggregate.py:179-181 (printed with every G7a verdict)
findings.quote: so among the four judged baselines only all_false is excluded by the constraints
findings.reason: G7a can fail only through all_false (echo, all_unknown and all_both cannot score; the oracle scores wherever it is feasible), so under a FAILS the sentence states the opposite of what happened. Under 'insufficient worlds' it asserts an exclusion without a verdict (my development run printed it so). all_false also scores 0 without any constraint where no H atom is world-false (new_true = 0); the gate's N7 minus world held on 7 of 100 development worlds.
findings.fix: '... only all_false can be excluded by the constraints.'

findings.quote: A WEAK certificate is accepted only with a written reason and the author's approval. / (a JSON object: study id → written reason)
findings.reason: The check also accepts a JSON list of ids, which carries no reason, and an empty reason. It waives any verdict (UNTESTED, NOT_FALSIFIABLE, UNDEFINED), not only WEAK. It matches the driver ids g1..g7, t1; a waiver keyed 'G7a' or 'T-1' waives nothing (fails safe, but not stated).
findings.fix: Accept only an object whose values are non-empty strings; waive only WEAK; state the id spelling in 6.3; add tests.

findings.quote: NT can hold on a world where the real new_false falls by at least 1/2 − 1/n_q
findings.reason: The condition for the extreme pair is a fall of at least 1/2 − max(delta, 1/n_q). On the power study's worlds n_q >= 20 at q on 14 553 of 18 796 T-1 pairs, where the term is delta. NT's gap (n_q in {1, 2} at the lowest-uncertainty feasible point) occurred on none of 1 684 defined world-draws.
findings.fix: '1/2 − max(δ, 1/n_q), n_q at the lowest-uncertainty feasible point'.

findings.quote: a single additional wrong conclusion never decides a pair
findings.reason: If the denominator falls from p to q and p already has a wrong conclusion, (a+1)/n_q − a/n_p > 1/n_q, so one extra wrong conclusion can exceed the tolerance. It never happened on development data (n_q fell on 0 of 18 796 pairs, recomputed), but that is an empirical result, not a property of the rule.
findings.fix: Add 'when the denominator does not fall from p to q (it fell on none of 18 796 development pairs)'.

findings.quote: τ, fidelity, deviation, consistency, uncertainty, new_true, new_false, n_q and the feasible set → T-1 and G7a
findings.reason: G7a never reads n_q, and a calibration world's n_q enters no tau and no test. Under the frozen map, a disagreement in n_q alone would still withdraw verdicts it cannot change.
findings.fix: Map a test world's n_q to T-1 only and a calibration world's n_q to none, in the text, the code and the tests.

findings.quote: In the other worlds, I at those α holds only T class atoms, so all_true contradicts no encoded atom and passes every constraint.
findings.reason: 24 worlds have no source >= 0.95, but all_true scored on 22. On 930001 and 930028, I is empty at alpha 0.95, so fidelity is undefined and the point is infeasible; at 0.90 their I holds non-T atoms and all_true is feasible under none of the 40 tau. The printed counts are correct.
findings.fix: 'In 22 of the 24 other worlds ...; in the other two, I is empty at 0.95'.
